comments: Gate 3 re-approved at artifactVersion 2, superseding the version 1 approval of 2026-09-01T13:00:00Z, which is preserved verbatim at features/generated/home-navigation/superseded/TP-ETA-411-001-automation-approval.v1.json. This decision was given by the reviewer in chat and transcribed into this artifact by the orchestrator; the transcription is a record of a human decision, not an agent approval. This is a narrow amendment, not a re-review of the whole automation design. Only TS-ETA-411-001 changed: the step 'And I have chosen to sign in on behalf of my organization' was added between the existing Given and When in features/approved/home-navigation/home-icon-navigation.feature. That step already exists in steps/organization-sign-in.steps.ts and is used seven times in ETA-351; no step definition, page object, component, fixture, test data or locator changed. AC-ETA-411-001 and TP-ETA-411-001 are untouched, so Gates 1 and 2 stay shut. The eight unchanged scenarios carry forward their version 1 decisions; their comments here have been rewritten to state what execution actually showed rather than what was anticipated at version 1, and the reviewer was told of that rewrite and accepted it. Verified before this gate was raised, so the decision is about legitimacy rather than function: bddgen regenerates cleanly to 11 tests with no undefined or duplicate steps, TS-ETA-411-001 passes in 35.6s, npm run typecheck is clean and npm run validate:artifacts reports 15 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped. Two things this approval does not do. It does not resolve AMB-ETA-411-006, which remains REVIEW_REQUIRED, so no scenario may reach the Preferences page by any route other than the Home page icon. It does not close the process gap the failure exposed: three gates, a design document, SEM-FEATURE-TAGS, SEM-AUTOMATION-HYGIENE and bddgen all passed a scenario that could never have worked, because nothing in the pipeline models the state a step requires on entry. That gap is recorded for the framework owner and is deliberately out of scope here.

itemDecisions.comment: Scenario: A successful organization sign-in places the user on the Home page. AMENDED at this version. Version 1 omitted the step that chooses organization sign-in, so 'When I sign in with correct organization details' filled a field the login page had not rendered and the scenario timed out after 30 seconds waiting on locator.fill. The login page only exposes the organization fields once the sign-in kind is chosen, which is the behaviour AC-ETA-351-003 exists to prove. The amendment restores the precondition that ETA-351 states in all seven of its uses. The scenario asserts exactly what it always asserted.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario: The Home page presents three activatable icons. Asserts presence and activatability only, and names the icons as the Home page dashboard icons rather than the header links of the same name. Rests on a single observed account - RISK-TP-ETA-411-004 stands. Passed at EXECUTION.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario: The New Transaction icon reaches the New Transaction page. Uses the dashboard icon, not the header link - the distinction from TS-ETA-411-008 is load-bearing and must survive any later refactor. Passed at EXECUTION, including the 'Create Transaction' heading assertion, which is the one genuine unique-element claim among the three destinations.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1 in the Gherkin, but the reviewer should know what happened underneath it. On 2026-09-01 EcoreWorkspacePage was strengthened to assert a visible heading named 'Search Criteria', on the strength of a validation probe that read textContent from legend and caption elements without checking ARIA role or visibility. No such heading exists; three scenarios failed and the reviewer reverted to the address-only assertion that TP-ETA-411-001 approved. The scenario text never changed. Arrival only, and AMB-ETA-411-002 stands: this will pass on a page that arrived and then failed to render.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario: The Preferences icon reaches the Preferences page. Arrival only, and the single approved route to this page while AMB-ETA-411-006 is open. Passed at EXECUTION. The page genuinely exposes nothing unique to it, so this assertion is knowingly weak.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario Outline: The Command Center control returns the user Home. All three return legs are walked rather than one walked and two inferred. Nothing is asserted about how the control is labelled - it exposes no accessible name, accepted as AMB-ETA-411-005. All three rows now pass. The Workspace row additionally required the Playwright test timeout to be raised from the 30s default to 90s, because sign-in plus a single Workspace navigation alone consumes 27.3s on qa1. That is a wall-clock budget, not a changed assertion; the expect timeout stays at 5s so a missing element still fails fast.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario: The header navigation offers New Transaction and Workspace links. Exactly two duplicates, not three, and this scenario must never be extended to claim a third. Passed at EXECUTION, and the captured accessibility snapshot independently confirms the header exposes Preferences as a plain list item with no link.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario: The header New Transaction link reaches the New Transaction page. The destination was unconfirmed when version 1 was approved; PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION has since walked it and it matches the approved expectation, so RISK-TP-ETA-411-001 is discharged for this scenario. Passed at EXECUTION.

UNCHANGED from artifactVersion 1. Scenario: The header Workspace link reaches the Workspace page. Destination since walked and confirmed, discharging RISK-TP-ETA-411-001 for this scenario too. Passed at EXECUTION once the false 'Search Criteria' assertion described under TS-ETA-411-004 was removed.
